newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden sees 12 bln Skr borrowing need 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sweden sees 12 bln Skr borrowing need 1997.

text.p: Sweden's national audit office said on Thursday it expected the government's borrowing requirement to amount to 12 billion crowns this year.
"The forecast includes (income of) 26 billion crowns deriving from the sale of government shares in Nordbanken ," the audit office said in a statement.
The government has not yet announced when or how it will sell its 59.4 percent stake in Nordbanken.
The forecast is 42 billion crowns lower than the government budget forecast and 25 billion crowns lower than the audit office's previous forecast, it said.

The audit office forecast government income would rise to 662.1 billion crowns, up 29.4 billion from its previous forecast, following the expected Nordbanken deal and the government sale of shares in mortgage lender Stadshypotek earlier this year for 7.6 billion crowns.

The office expected government expenses to rise to 674.4 billion crowns, up 4.1 billion crowns from its earlier forecast partly because the government has proposed to spend another four billion crowns on municipalities.
Higher interest rates and a softer crown are expected to increase costs for some interest rate payments on state debt by 3.2 billion crowns compared to the previous forecast, the audit office said.
The gap between total expenditures and the spending ceiling amounts to nine billion crowns, narrowing by 1.4 billion crowns since the last forecast.
Positive one-time effects are seen at 62.3 billion crowns compared to 89.9 billion crowns in 1996.
